I will keep my land in the usual wheat and summer maize rotation. I am in Quzhou County, and for me this is the safest way to earn grain and keep the work manageable. I know this system well, the local weather fits it, and I do not want to take extra risk on crops that need more labor, more market chasing, or more complicated management. Since it is the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will manage that to harvest first, then I will turn the same land straight into summer maize.

For wheat, I will focus on steady water and fertilizer, not excessive input. I will use improved wheat seed, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate a few key times, and spray only when pests or disease pressure rises. After wheat harvest, I will move fast so I do not lose summer moisture. I will use hybrid maize on the same area because it gives me stable yield. I will keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate at the important stages if the rain is short, and control weeds and insects with limited but timely sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and fits quick turnover between the two crops.
